note.note:
Consult Summary:
- Video consult for 6-week intermittent left-sided hearing reduction with unilateral tinnitus and mild episodic imbalance; plan is in-person otoscopic exam to exclude cerumen impaction/physical blockage and provide tinnitus education.

History:
- Presenting complaint/timeline: Left-sided reduced hearing for ~6 weeks, intermittent. Similar brief episode ~1 year ago lasting a couple of days.
- Associated symptoms: Unilateral tinnitus (left). Intermittent mild dizziness/off-balance; not true spinning vertigo; minimal/no nausea. Right ear seems normal.
- Potential triggers: Patient reports symptoms associated with watching TV/listening to music (wording unclear whether triggers or alleviates).
- Pertinent negatives: No ear pain, no ear discharge, no fever reported. No chest pain, no palpitations. Denies using cotton buds to clean ears.
- Past medical history/Allergies/Medications: Not discussed.
- Social/preventive: Not discussed.

Examination:
- Telehealth visit; no vitals obtained.
- No physical exam performed; no otoscopy yet.

Impression:
- Working clinical impression: Unilateral left hearing difficulty with tinnitus and mild disequilibrium.
  - Most likely to exclude first: Cerumen impaction or other external/middle ear blockage (consistent with painless unilateral muffled hearing; plan aligns with clinician’s approach to rule out simple causes).
  - Other considerations if otoscopy is normal:
    - Eustachian tube dysfunction/otitis media with effusion (fits fluctuating, painless unilateral symptoms).
    - Early Ménière disease (unilateral tinnitus, fluctuating symptoms, episodic imbalance), though absence of true vertigo/aural fullness is less typical.
    - Less likely: Vestibular schwannoma, given short time course and age; consider only if persistent/unexplained after initial evaluation.

Plan:
- Arrange face-to-face appointment within 4–5 days for otoscopic examination to check for wax/physical obstruction and assess tympanic membrane.
- Provide tinnitus information leaflet link in visit notes; patient to review prior to appointment.
- Patient instructed to call support team (number provided in visit notes) to schedule the in-person visit.
- Safety-net: If symptoms worsen or new concerns arise before the appointment, book another appointment/video review.

Quality checks:
- Missing expected elements: Past medical history, medication list, allergies, vitals, otoscopic findings, formal hearing assessment (audiometry), neurological exam details, specific follow-up plan contingent on otoscopy results.
- Conflicts: Transcript wording suggests TV/music “trigger” the tinnitus, but one phrase reads “solve the ringing” (ambiguity noted). DDx assumes sound-triggered symptoms; transcript is unclear—conflict/ambiguity noted.
- Transcript quality: Incomplete responses at times; minor transcription ambiguities; no physical exam available via video.
